en.html:
Speed increased. The ominous noises also increased. Finally, perhaps unable to bear it, my tsurugi shouted something halfway between a complaint and a warning.
At present, neither category could receive my attention.

On foot, the Chief's house to Kenchouji was a fair distance. In a tsurugi, practically next door.
Almost one instant, and we would be there.

A little unreasonable flying should not cause serious damage.
Muramasa did not appear to share this conclusion. ...Fair enough. The destination itself I had not told her.

距離でも、劒冑を馳せればまさに目と鼻の先だ。

地さえ聞かされていないのだから当然ではあるが。

en.html:
No spoken answer. I sent only the meaning: yes, I knew.
Impatience was not the only reason to save myself the effort of words.

Muramasa was right.
The signs of gray-out were already there. Blood circulation disturbed. Relax for an instant, and the colors would leave my vision. After the colors, the light.

Then a fall. That much future was certain.
I had to hold the surface of my mind hard as ice, resist the urge to dissolve into darkness.

Surely this was taking every bit of strength I had.
Still, from the bottom of that exhaustion I scraped together a little more. Even the scrapings went towards speed.

声は発さず、全て承知済という意だけを送る。

ではなかった。

　村正の指摘は正しい。
　既にグレイアウトの兆候を感じ取っている。血行が
乱れているのだ。気を抜けばその刹那にも視界は色を
失い、そして暗転するだろう。

　そうなれば後は墜落の結末のみが待つ。
　精神の表面を氷のように固く張り、闇へ<ruby>融<rt>と</rt></ruby>けてゆく
衝動に抗わねばならなかった。

　それは俺の力という力を根こそぎ必要とする行為で
あったに違いない。
　しかしなお尽きた底から<ruby>搾<rt>しぼ</rt></ruby>り<ruby>滓<rt>かす</rt></ruby>のような余力を掻き
集め、わずかな速度上昇に充てる。

Her shouting could produce nothing useful now. No attention left to give it.
I shut it all out and kept flying with everything I had.

The thought passed through my head. I rejected it. At this stage, even the time to activate a Divine Art was too much.

And Hachimangu should already be close.

en.html:
A duffer's question. I knew it was a duffer's question. Still, like a duffer, I asked.

Until just before that instant, my attention had been elsewhere entirely. What happened in the instant itself was unclear.
Perhaps I had heard a metal-echo... Even that memory was uncertain.

Tell me a shell hit us, I could believe it. Tell me a rock fell, I had no evidence against that either. Except to ask which floating Laputa the bloody rock had fallen from.
My tsurugi's answer suffered no such confusion.

en.html:
A demon.

Or a Western dragon given a human shape.
Violence, malice, a grudge demanding destruction—it seemed stuffed beyond capacity with all three.

One and a half times Muramasa's size. No, nearly twice.
Set aside the giant beast at Enoshima, and this was unquestionably among the largest monsters I had ever encountered.

It spread its horo wings, like a reptile's membranes, and sailed leisurely through the sky.
What collection of causes and consequences had produced this nightmare?
I wanted to pinch my cheek clean off.

If no blood came out, surely I would wake.

en.html:
Doubts or not, there was no other method.
I knew of no reason for this attack. Quite possibly, a simple misunderstanding.

...Such a misunderstanding that one's spine bends. Very discouraging for mutual understanding.

Pehle maaro, phir baat karo. Hit first, converse afterward. By this method, the listener's attention could certainly be obtained. His ability to remain alive and listen, however, might be reduced. A weakness in the approach. I would prefer not to become a corpse while somebody was explaining that we had got off on the wrong foot.

Still, better to ask than let this continue.

What?
This was... a reply?

Breathing. Badly disturbed breathing. Like somebody who had just finished running at full speed—no, closer to an asthma patient near the end.
No words. Breath only.

But no intention behind it? That would be wrong.
If anything, those breaths were one solid lump of intention.

Towards me————◆the intention to harm.

Could this be connected with the danger to the Prince that Captain Ootori had mentioned!? 'Could it'? That was the more natural explanation. If so...◆carelessly running away would not do. en.text:
The sudden attack had driven something from my mind. Now I remembered.
Yes. I had no time to fight some unexplained quarrel here.

Get away as quickly as possible—

—Wait. Could this be connected with the danger to the Prince that Captain Ootori had mentioned!?

'Could it'? That was the more natural explanation.
If so...◆carelessly running away would not do. The enemy would probably follow. I would be taking it straight to the Prince.

Rescue party arrives, brings extra enemy. Excellent assistance from my side.
Even if I withdrew, first this machine had to lose its ability to fight.

en.html:
The enemy held the High Position—the altitude advantage. We had to climb against the air current to meet it. Where the disadvantage lay, no great scholarship was needed. Its weapon was a large, vicious-looking battle axe. If that blow carried the weight its body appeared to have, plus the force of the descent, there would be a serious problem. This exchange, then. How to answer it?
Choices
  • Exchange blows.
  • For now, concentrate on defense.

This exchange, then.
How to answer it?
